MANILA, Philippines – Shifting to a refreshed identity, the newly christened Gilas Hiraya looks to bear the fruit of the hoop-crazy nation’s hopes, dreams, and aspirations in a huge 2027.
Gilas Hiraya, the new name of the Philippine women’s basketball team, was unveiled this month to establish its own identity as an emerging force in Asian hoops.

The rebrand comes ahead of a pivotal year in which both the 3×3 and 5-on-5 squads will chase a spot in the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, alongside the country’s hosting of the FIBA Women’s Asia Cup at the SM Seaside Arena in Cebu next year.
“It’s really a deliberate decision to give them an identity of their own in order to shape a pathway that is unique for them,” Samahang Basketbol ng Pilipinas (SBP) executive director Erika Dy said.
“We don’t want them to just follow the footsteps of the men’s team or the men’s program,” she added. “We want them to be able to create their own dreams and aspirations for Philippine basketball.”
According to Dy, the idea of giving the women’s team its own name was suggested by FIBA secretary general Andreas Zagklis during a meeting in Shenzhen, China, in July 2025.
Zagklis pushed for the rebrand upon learning that the women’s team used to be known as “Perlas Pilipinas” before aligning its identity with the broader Gilas Pilipinas program in 2019.

Following lengthy discussions with numerous stakeholders, including the UAAP and the players themselves, Hiraya stood out among the other shortlisted names and was officially picked by the SBP on October 27.
“Part of why we chose the word Hiraya, which represents dreams, hopes, and aspirations — it’s a deep Tagalog word,” explained Dy, herself a former basketball player and coach for Ateneo.
“It’s because we really believe that our women’s program can represent that for all the women in the Philippines. It actually goes beyond basketball.”
With a fresh identity, Gilas Hiraya is riding a wave of sustained success, buoyed by a 3×3 silver-medal finish at the Asian Games and a deep tournament run by the 5-on-5 squad in the same meet.
Helping lead the way are Asiad silver medalists Kacey dela Rosa of Ateneo and Amyah Español of Far Eastern University.

“I’m just grateful that we have our own identity now as a women’s basketball team. And I just think every player on the women’s team is very dedicated to growing the sport of women’s basketball in the Philippines,” said Español.
“I’m just thankful that we have such a great support system who believes in us to have our own identity as the women’s team.”
For Dela Rosa, a two-time UAAP MVP, the identity shift reflects the program’s continued development under program director Bacon Austria and head coach BT Toews.

“As Filipinos, we put in a lot of work, like hard work, and we want them to know how much hard work we put in and sacrifices outside the court,” Dela Rosa said. “We also want them to recognize us — we are a team that dreams big.” – Rappler.com
